body.statement:
For every fixed \(c>0\), every \(P\) satisfying \(\mathrm{ass{:}positive\text{-}observed\text{-}cells}\), and every \(\Delta\), the independently model-defined legal fibers obey
\[
 (\log c,\Delta)\in\Theta_{\mathrm w}(P)
 \Longleftrightarrow\mathcal F_c^{\mathrm w}(P,\Delta)\ne\varnothing,
 \qquad
 (\log c,\Delta)\in\Theta_+(P)
 \Longleftrightarrow\mathcal F_c^+(P,\Delta)\ne\varnothing.
\]
The weak certificate uses exactly fifty-six scalar lift variables, eight \(3\times3\) PSD blocks, and eight augmented \(4\times4\) PSD blocks; the strict certificate uses sixty-four variables and eight additional \(6\times6\) common-Hankel-range blocks.  In the forward direction, each legal \((\mu,h,g)\in\mathcal M_v(c)\) is mapped to the eight joint response measures \(d\nu_{(x,r_0,r_1)}=h_xg_{x0}(r_0,\cdot)g_{x1}(r_1,\cdot)d\mu\), and then to \(d\rho_s=D_c^{-1}d\nu_s\) and its five quartic moments.  In the reverse direction, every feasible lift yields positive-half-line representing measures \((\rho_s)_{s\in S}\); after setting \(d\nu_s=D_c d\rho_s\), the construction \(\mu=\sum_{s\in S}\nu_s\) and the Radon--Nikodym reconstructions produce one unconditional probability law together with legal sequential initial and feedback kernels that generate exactly \(P\) and \(\Delta\).  For \(v=+\), the common-Hankel-range blocks yield representing measures on one positive-node set with strictly positive type weights, so the reconstructed \(h_x\) and \(g_{xy}\) satisfy the strict legal class.  When \(q_x>0\), the weak equivalence is an exact finite-dimensional representation of the \(T=2\) Bonhomme--Dano--Graham unrestricted-feedback, unrestricted-measure fiber after adjoining the observed margins \(q_x\) and applying the conditional-law translation in \(\mathrm{lem{:}bdg\text{-}weak\text{-}fiber\text{-}translation}\).  The strict fiber is an additional subclass, not a second copy of that weak published fiber.  Here unrestricted heterogeneity means an arbitrary probability law on the continuous state space \((0,\infty)\); exact correspondence with a separately imposed Lebesgue-density specialization would require an additional absolutely-continuous representation theorem and is not established by the atomic converse.
body.justification: This is now the positive-cell, hence positive-margin, Bonhomme--Dano--Graham comparison corollary of the all-laws theorem.
body.gap: The all-laws construction and zero-cell exactness live in thm:exact-feedback-cone-all-laws; this node isolates comparator scope and the density caveat.
body.consumer: It connects the finite certificate to the published conditional weak fiber without extending that attribution to the strict class.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(c>0\), a probability vector \(P\) satisfying \(\mathrm{ass{:}positive\text{-}observed\text{-}cells}\), and \(\Delta\in\mathbb R\).  The two equivalences follow immediately from \(\mathrm{thm{:}exact\text{-}feedback\text{-}cone\text{-}all\text{-}laws}\), whose hypotheses require only \(P\in\Delta^{15}\).  Thus the finite feasibility sets equal the independently model-defined causal fibers; they are not definitions of those fibers and are not outer approximations.

For each \(x\in B\), positivity of the eight cells having first coordinate \(x\) implies
\[
 q_x=\sum_{y,z,w\in B}P(x,y,z,w)>0. \tag{1}
\]
The positive-margin hypothesis of \(\mathrm{lem{:}bdg\text{-}weak\text{-}fiber\text{-}translation}\) is therefore satisfied.  That lemma normalizes \(h_xd\mu\) by \(q_x\) in the forward direction and, in the reverse direction, mixes the conditional laws with weights \(q_x\) and recovers \(h_x\) by a Radon--Nikodym derivative.  It preserves every path probability and the unconditional APE, so it proves the stated equality with the conditional-on-\(X_1\), unrestricted-measure weak fiber.

The precise published and present scopes are given by \(\mathrm{lem{:}bdg\text{-}continuous\text{-}feedback\text{-}program}\).  Independently, the inclusion \(\mathcal M_+(c)\subseteq\mathcal M_{\mathrm w}(c)\) follows directly from \(\mathrm{def{:}strict\text{-}legal\text{-}class}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}weak\text{-}legal\text{-}class}\), so the strict fiber is an additional subclass.  The translation preserves arbitrary probability measures, including atomic and mixed measures, and no declared theorem replaces them by Lebesgue-density representations.  This proves every comparison and scope assertion.
